title: Museum of Old and New Art
geometryBasis: Original museum 19-point shell and roof outline, separately mapped Courtyard House, Pharos, Round House, stair and ferry pier. The named site geometry is divided into roof, exposed front and river approach.
sectionBasis: The riverfront photos show repeated grille fields framed by tapering rusty steel, a mostly concealed rear, glass and white plaster buildings above the terrace, and a stair down to the shore. The 17 m museum section is used only as scale evidence.
limitations: The shell positions and cuts are approximate within the independently mapped volume. The front bay proportions are derived from the river views. Exact roof levels, grille details, the nearby lower quay structures and Pharos and Round House finishes are estimates.
The terrain is the original rotated Tasmanian elevation field, including the riverbed. Cut edges, waterline and terrace contact are approximate and we apply no changes to the terrain.

The modeled scope covers the above-grade architecture and waterfront approach. Underground interiors, held art, exterior installations, winery, lodges and other detached estate structures are outside scope.
